land.text: Memphis and the Delta, which the Kushite pharaohs had held

predecessors.note: Lower Egypt passed between Kush and Assyria in 671, 669, 667, 664 and 663 (kingdom-of-kush and neo-assyrian-empire dossiers).

land.text: the Delta, where "Over all of Egypt, I appointed kings, viceroys, governors" (Esarhaddon, 671)

predecessors.note: Egypt is a vassal of the Neo-Assyrian Empire from 664 (its vassal_start/vassal_end events).

land.text: all of Egypt under Psamtik I, independent from about 655

successors.note: Cliopatria starts its Twenty-sixth Dynasty row in -615; Psamtik I was king from 664 and independent from about 655 (Assyrian conquest of Egypt page).

capitals.name: Sais (Sa el-Hagar)
capitals.note: Esarhaddon "established Necho I as king at Sais"; Psamtik I, Necho I's successor, ruled from Sais; the page does not say so for 664-655, so the seat is the reading of the Sais line.

correction.text: Lower Egypt, the Delta and Memphis, under the vassal king Psamtik I

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -664..-657: the Delta and Memphis under Psamtik I, the Assyrian vassal king: "He installed a native Egyptian Pharaoh, Psammetichus, as a vassal king in 664 BCE"; "Tantamani's authority was still recognized in Upper Egypt until his 8th Year in 656 BCE". The page does not say which areas Assyria held directly.

correction.text: all of Egypt from the Delta to Thebes under Psamtik I

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -656..-655: Egypt united under the still-Assyrian vassal: "Psamtik I's navy peacefully took control of Thebes" in 656, and "Psamtik I threw off his ties to the Assyrians circa 655 BCE". Valid for the last two years of the dossier.

correction.text: Egypt only, valid -650..-655; later years belong to the Twenty-sixth Dynasty

keyframe_review.note: 1,255,946 km2 (-650..-631) is the whole Neo-Assyrian Empire (4,503 of its 4,508 cells lie inside the Neo-Assyrian -675 shape; Egypt alone is about 404,000 km2). The pages show Egypt vassal only to c. 655: "Egypt already regained independence in the middle of Ashurbanipal's reign" (Ashurbanipal page). Use the Egypt of the new keyframes for -650..-655 and the twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt dossier after.

correction.text: Egypt, independent under Psamtik I; belongs to twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt

keyframe_review.note: 1,435,218 km2 (-630..-616) is again the whole empire (the Neo-Assyrian infobox gives 1,400,000 km2 for 670) and Egypt was independent: the page says nothing of Assyrian control after about 655, only that the Saite dynasty "remained on friendly terms with them". Not usable for this state; the years belong to the twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt dossier (Egypt), with the Assyrian remainder in neo-assyrian-empire_-655.

ledger.note: 664 BC: Psamtik I becomes Assyria's vassal king in Egypt. "He installed a native Egyptian Pharaoh, Psammetichus, as a vassal king in 664 BCE" (Ashurbanipal page: "After becoming king in 664 as a loyal Assyrian vassal"). Necho I had been set at Sais by Esarhaddon in 671; Tantamani still held Upper Egypt.

region.text: Upper Egypt from Thebes, "peacefully taking control of the still rebellious Upper Egypt"

ledger.note: 656 BC: Psamtik I takes Thebes. "Tantamani's authority was still recognized in Upper Egypt until his 8th Year in 656 BCE, when Psamtik I's navy peacefully took control of Thebes"; Ashurbanipal page: he unified the country "in 656".

c. 655 BC: Egypt is independent. "Psamtik I threw off his ties to the Assyrians circa 655 BCE"; "By 656/655 BCE, this vassal king was able to declare outright independence." The Twenty-sixth Dynasty continues the land.

wars.name: Psamtik I's reunification and break with Assyria

zones.text: Upper Egypt, taken peacefully at Thebes

wars.outcome: Psamtik I's navy took Thebes in 656 without a fight and he declared independence c. 655; "he recruited mercenaries from Caria and ancient Greece".

wars.name: Assyrian conquest of Egypt

zones.text: Egypt from the Delta to Thebes

wars.outcome: Assyrian victory: Memphis 671, the Delta back to Taharqa 669, Ashurbanipal 667, Psammetichus vassal 664, Tantamani beaten 663; "vassalised Egypt for a period of about 10 years".
wars.note: Full ledger in neo-assyrian-empire and kingdom-of-kush.

certainty.note: Which parts of Egypt Assyria held directly and which through the vassal kings is not on the page.

sources.title: Assyrian conquest of Egypt
sources.note: 673-663 conquest, Necho I at Sais, Psammetichus vassal king 664, Thebes taken peacefully by Psamtik I 656, independence c. 655. No area.

sources.title: Ashurbanipal
sources.note: Psamtik I king in 664 as a loyal Assyrian vassal, unified the country in 656; Egypt independent in the middle of Ashurbanipal's reign.

notes:
WHAT THIS ROW IS. Cliopatria's "Assyrian Egypt" (-650..-616, Wikidata Q97357417 = the article "Assyrian conquest of Egypt") is the whole Neo-Assyrian Empire again: 4,503 of its 4,508 cells at -650 lie inside Cliopatria's Neo-Assyrian -675 shape, and the -630 shape adds 48,810 km2 on the east side (to 50.4 E). Both shapes are marked wrong. The state this dossier describes instead is Egypt under Assyrian vassal kings, 664 to c. 655, type colony. The map should draw Assyria and Egypt through the neo-assyrian-empire and twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt dossiers, and drop this row for -654..-616.
CONFLICTS. Cliopatria's Assyrian rule over Egypt to -616 (34 years) vs the page's about 10 years of vassalage (673-663) and independence c. 655; the Twenty-sixth Dynasty in Cliopatria starts -615, 40 years after Psamtik's independence: the me-03 dossier should start in -664 or -655. The kingdom-of-kush dossier books the -656 loss of Upper Egypt to this slug; mirrored by the gain here. NA's direct holdings in Lower Egypt in 671-663 (kush mirrors) overlap this state's Delta from 664.
PAGES. 2 pages (budget 1-2): Assyrian conquest of Egypt, Ashurbanipal (both shared with neo-assyrian-empire). No infobox area for Egypt. The capital is a reading (Sais).
NOT SETTLED. Whether Memphis was Assyrian or Psamtik's in 664-663; which Delta principalities (Sais, Mendes, Pelusium) were separate vassals (the page lists them in 665) rather than one kingdom.
